paragraphs: Alcatraz makes facial authentication products that work with the badge readers and access control systems an organization already runs. The device, called Rock X, sits in line between the badge reader and the access control panel over Wiegand or OSDP.

Employees enroll at a station, remotely from a browser or phone, or automatically after repeated badge swipes at a door fitted with the device. Authentication happens on the device itself, and the company states that no sensitive data is stored or transmitted. Profiles are anonymized and tied to the badge ID already held in the customer's access control system. The same unit can act as a passive second factor, so a person badges in as usual and the face confirms the match. In lobbies it can be built directly into certain turnstiles. The management platform runs on premise or in the cloud.

Airports are one setting the company writes about, pairing face recognition with badges or PINs to add a second factor at restricted doors. One unnamed case summary on the site describes a global enterprise that put the device on turnstiles for more than 150,000 employees. The company says its approach helps customers conform with privacy regulations such as BIPA, CCPA and GDPR.

quote.text: authentication happens at the edge ensuring no sensitive data is stored or transmitted
